thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging sara (oncall) and eng-sre. High error spike and token queueing observed for route `text.generate` in eu-west-1. 95th latency > 4s, throughput dropping. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/1769456789

sara: seeing it, joining. what's the customer impact?

olivia: CS: multiple paid customers reporting timeouts on chat widgets in EU. A couple escalations flagged as priority.

aj: oncall here. quick check: is this capacity saturation or network blip?

maria: logs show KV cache misses jumped ~3x and GPU utilization at 98% on pool-eu-a. Also a spike in long-sequence requests from a handful of tenants.

sanjay: looks like a mix: a single customer sent large batch inference jobs hitting long context lengths. They're on paid+burst.

kevin: if that's true we should isolate them and do a per-tenant throttle to stop tail latency from dragging others.

aj: agree. proposed mitigations (short): 1) apply temporary tiered routing so free-tier and low-SLA customers get routed to a lower-cost model variant or throttled 2) steer non-EU traffic to us-west if latency still OK 3) bump quotas for critical paid customers 4) disable non-essential features (tool-calling / complex plugins) for high-cost requests

olivia: CS ok with temporary QoS changes but need message template for customers affected.

incident-bot: mitigation checklist created: INC-1769456789. Assigning to aj.

aj: I'm going to apply a smart-routing override to prefer us-west for routes where client region != EU and customer_tier != premium. Command: 
```
# apply routing override
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/routing/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"match": "region!=eu-west-1 && tier!=premium", "prefers": "us-west-2", "weight": 0.8, "expires_in": 900}'
```

maria: also flipping per-tenant ratecap on the noisy customer (tenant-id: tn-8423) to 30 rps and max tokens 20000. Using admin CLI: 
```
redwoodctl tenants update tn-8423 --ratecap 30 --token-cap 20000
```

sanjay: will that break their current jobs? need to notify them first.

aj: we can put them in throttled mode with a header advising retry-after. I'll send an automated email + slack to their account rep. olivia pls coordinate.

olivia: on it. drafting: "We're applying a short quota throttle to prevent wider service disruption. Expect degraded throughput up to 15 minutes. We'll follow up."

kevin: we should also enable prefix caching more aggressively for common prompts to reduce recompute. That's a config flip on the runtime: 
```
# enable aggressive prefix caching
redwoodctl runtime config set --pool pool-eu-a --prefix-cache aggressive
```

aj: doing the routing override now. Pasting response...

deploy-bot: routing-override applied id=rov-9921 by aj at 2026-03-15T10:12:05Z

aj: override in. traffic to us-west increased by ~40% within the first minute, overall tail latency improved to 2.1s but eu-west core still elevated.

maria: I applied tenant throttle for tn-8423. They hit the limit, jobs queued. Their rep acknowledges.

olivia: notified customers. rep for tn-8423 replies: "we're running overnight evals, can you whitelist?"

aj: for critical customers we can do a manual quota bump. who needs immediate support?

olivia: two customers: tn-1122 (enterprise) and tn-5066 (payments). tn-1122 already on premium; they need consistent latency.

aj: I'll issue temporary token increase for those tenants for 30 minutes. Command: 
```
redwoodctl tenants update tn-1122 --ratecap 200 --token-cap 100000 --expires 1800
```

kevin: while this buys time, let's push a soft-degradation rule for non-critical features: no function-calls on free and standard tiers in eu until load normalizes.

maria: applied feature gate: 
```
feature-gate set function-calls --region eu-west-1 --tiers free,standard --state disabled --expires 900
```
deploy-bot: feature-gate applied id=fg-2234 by maria

aj: summary so far: routing override to us-west (rov-9921), tenant throttle for tn-8423, quota bumps for tn-1122 & tn-5066, disabled function-calls for free/standard in EU, enabled aggressive prefix caching. Latency trending down but still noisy.

sara: i'm going to take a 30m break in 10 and handoff to aj formally. aj, can you take the incident lead and run the postmortem timeline?

aj: taking lead. I'll declare an incident bridge and add runbook steps. Creating bridge now.

incident-bot: conference bridge created: https://zoom.us/j/incident-1769456789

maria: note — autoscaler logs show delayed scale-up due to quota exhaustion in the eu account; we should check quota backfills for gpu-pool scaling. Might need manual scale.

kevin: i'm provisioning an extra GPU node in pool-eu-a as emergency capacity. Command: 
```
infractl pool scale pool-eu-a +1 --reason "INC-1769456789 emergency"
```
deploy-bot: node provisioning started id=node-78

aj: good. once node comes up we'll reduce routing override weight and re-enable features incrementally.

olivia: CS asked for an ETA to tell customers — recommend 30-60 minutes.

aj: agreed. posting customer update now.

olivia: posted. tn-1122 says thanks. tn-8423 requests a follow-up postmortem; flagged.

sara: handing off formally to aj. I'm going offline now — ping me if it escalates.

aj: acknowledged. handoff noted. Current owner: aj. Next update in 10.

incident-bot: INC-1769456789 status=mitigated actions=6 assignee=aj

kevin: node-78 is online and joining pool. GPU util down to 85%, tail latency now ~1.6s.

maria: rolling back some of the aggressive measures: increasing routing weight back to default, re-enabling function-calls for standard tier (still keep free tier disabled).

deploy-bot: routing-override updated id=rov-9921 weight=0.2 by maria

aj: monitoring. if metrics stable for 30m we'll close incident and start postmortem. thanks all.

olivia: prepping customer post-incident note and follow-up survey.

sara: back briefly — thanks for the handoff, solid playbook.

aj: thanks team. I'll capture timeline and action items for the postmortem doc.

incident-bot: INC-1769456789 will be transitioned to postmortem queue after 30m of stable metrics."
